cohort: The study analyzed 180 pregnant women diagnosed with asthma, who were hospitalized and delivered at a single center between September 1, 2019, and December 1, 2021, divided into mild asthma (n=160) and uncontrolled asthma (n=20) groups.
finding: Uncontrolled asthma during pregnancy is associated with significantly higher rates of adverse maternal-fetal and neonatal outcomes compared to mild asthma.
